key_insight: A vision–language–action model trained on a large, instruction-annotated driving dataset (InstructScene) can directly map natural language instructions plus visual inputs to driving trajectories, enabling flexible, personalized driving behaviors.
problem_solved: Existing driving pipelines treat language mainly as scene description or for reasoning and cannot flexibly follow diverse user instructions; this work enables instruction-conditioned decision-making for personalized autonomous driving.
method: Build InstructScene: a large-scale dataset (~100k scenes) pairing diverse natural-language driving instructions with corresponding trajectories/actions.
Train a unified vision–language–action model that conditions on onboard perception (images/scene) and a user instruction to predict trajectories or control commands.
Learn multimodal alignment between language and trajectory via instruction-conditioned objectives so the policy executes different behaviors based on varied instructions.
impact: Provides a practical route to instruction-following autonomous driving and a new benchmark for multimodal control research, making it easier for practitioners to develop personalized, language-driven vehicle policies.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: camera + user text → vision–language–action model → predicted trajectory/actions
Dataset summary card: sample scenes, example instructions (e.g., “take the next left”, “overtake slowly”), and scale (~100k scenes)
Instruction-conditioned examples: side-by-side trajectories showing different behaviors for the same scene under different instructions
Evaluation/ablation sketch: bar or radar chart comparing instruction-following performance across instruction types or model variants
paper_title: Vega: Learning to Drive with Natural Language Instructions
paper_authors: Sicheng Zuo, Yuxuan Li, Wenzhao Zheng, Zheng Zhu, Jie Zhou
